transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-26 16:00 UTC | Duration: 56 minutes | Recording: yes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Sam (Redwood SE), Lena (Redwood CSM), Jordan (Polaris Head of Security), Maya (Polaris Platform Eng), Ravi (Polaris Privacy Counsel), Nina (Polaris DevOps)

Summary: quick security review focused on data handling, prompt retention, PII/PHI controls, KMS and 'no training' assurances, plus SSO/RBAC and audit logs. Next: share SOC2/ISO docs, run pilot scoping, follow-up technical deep dive.

00:00 Alex: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, uh i'll do a 2 minute intro then hand to sam for the architecture bits.
00:14 Jordan: thanks, alex; appreciate it. main goal today: we need explicit confirmation on how prompt data is handled, whether any customer content is used to train models, and our options for KMS and data residency — plus retention windows for audit logs.
00:29 Alex: yep, clear. quick note — i'm alex kim, your AE, and sam patel is our solutions engineer. lena's on for next steps.
00:37 Sam: mm-hmm, i'll start with a high-level, then we can drill into KMS/keys and retention. so Redwood offers hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. hosted API is multi-tenant, dedicated is reserved capacity with tenant isolation and optional customer-managed keys, private is VPC / on-prem.
00:55 Maya: can you confirm hosted mode's data usage policy? specifically, do you train models on customer prompts?
01:02 Sam: short answer: no, redwood does not use customer prompts or content to train our public model weights. i want to be explicit — we do not incorporate customer data into model training or improvement pipelines. that policy is in our security docs; we'll share the SOC2 and the policy link.
01:20 Ravi: is that for both hosted and dedicated? like any telemetry or aggregated signals?
01:27 Sam: for hosted and dedicated we maintain the same no-training promise. we may collect telemetry for service performance (latency, error rates) but that's operational metrics and is not fed into model training. any aggregated telemetry is anonymized and used strictly for product quality.
01:41 Jordan: and for Private deployments?
01:44 Sam: private deployments are customer-managed; by default nothing leaves your VPC and we don't have access unless you grant it. so certainly no training.
01:53 Nina: ok good. how about prompt retention — if a user sends PHI in a prompt, how long is the content stored?
02:00 Sam: hosted mode defaults to a short retention for troubleshooting logs — by default 30 days for request logs and 90 days for audit logs, but we have options to turn off request content retention; you can configure retention or enable automatic redaction. for Dedicated and Private you can set retention to meet compliance, and for Private you control logs entirely. we'll send the retention matrix.
02:20 Jordan: retention matrix would be great. on PII/PHI handling, do you offer redaction or auto-detection?
02:26 Sam: yes, we have out-of-box PII detection pipelines that can mask certain classes of data, and you can integrate with your own preprocessing to remove PHI before sending. for highly regulated workloads we recommend Dedicated or Private with customer-managed KMS and stricter retention.
02:40 Maya: customer-managed KMS — can you integrate with AWS KMS and bring-your-own-keys?
02:45 Sam: yes. Dedicated supports CMK via AWS KMS, and we also support Google KMS and Azure Key Vault in Dedicated. For Private we support customer-managed keys and HSM when deployed on-prem. encryption at rest is AES-256 and in-transit is TLS1.2/1.3.
02:59 Ravi: do you have BYOK with HSM-backed keys? we need key isolation for PHI.
03:05 Sam: yes, HSM-backed keys are supported for Private deployments; for Dedicated we can offer customer-managed keys via cloud KMS with strict key policies. we'll include the KMS/HSM integration notes.
03:17 Jordan: audit logs — retention and tamper-evidence?
03:21 Sam: audit logs are immutable once written, stored with write-once patterns and integrity hashes. default retention in hosted is 90 days but can extend to one year or longer with add-on. Dedicated customers can set retention; Private you control. logs include request id, user id, model used, route, timestamps, and redacted prompt by default if configured.
03:41 Nina: and access to logs — RBAC? SSO?
03:44 Alex: yes we have RBAC in the Console, SSO via SAML and OIDC, SCIM for user provisioning, and audit trails for admin actions. roles are configurable and can be mapped to your IDP groups.
03:56 Jordan: do you support session-level keys or short-lived tokens?
03:59 Sam: short-lived tokens are supported via our token service and we recommend rotating long-lived API keys. For Dedicated and Private you can integrate with your identity provider for federated auth.
04:12 Maya: what about segmentation of data between customers in Dedicated — is there any co-mingling?
04:18 Sam: Dedicated uses tenant isolation at the runtime layer, separate storage namespaces, and network segmentation. no co-mingling of customer data across tenants; we also have process and penetration testing to validate.
04:29 Jordan: penetration testing — do you provide reports or can we run our own?
04:33 Alex: we do annual third-party pentests and will share a summary; for enterprise customers we can arrange a tailored assessment or on-site demo.
04:42 Ravi: encryption certificates and key rotation policies?
04:45 Sam: key rotation can be automated with KMS; we recommend a rotation cadence that matches your policy. we'll send our key management policy excerpt.
04:54 Jordan: i want to get explicit language for our legal team — can you confirm "redwood will not use customer data to improve or retrain models" in writing?
05:02 Alex: yes, we'll provide a written statement in the security pack: "Redwood does not use customer prompts, outputs, or other customer-provided content to train, improve, or refine model weights or underlying training datasets." we'll include that exact wording in the docs we send.
05:19 Ravi: any exceptions like opt-in feedback?
05:22 Sam: opt-in is possible but only with explicit customer consent and contractual terms; it's not on by default.
05:28 Maya: how about data residency — our data must stay in eu-west-1 for pilot. you have eu regions?
05:33 Sam: yes, we have hosted regions in eu-west-1 and eu-central-1; Dedicated can be provisioned in those regions; Private obviously runs in your infra. we'll note eu-west-1 for the pilot.
05:46 Nina: retention of prompts when using streaming responses — do you store intermediate tokens?
05:50 Sam: streaming is handled in-memory where possible; we persist final request/response pairs to logs if retention is enabled. intermediate token buffer is not persisted by default.
05:59 Jordan: curious about developer tools — are prompts cached for batching? does that affect privacy?
06:04 Sam: batching can use prefix cache (KV cache) to reduce cost — caching is per-tenant in Dedicated and Private; caching behavior is configurable and you can disable caches if that conflicts with privacy needs.
06:16 Jordan: are there any known gaps in your SOC2 compliance related to model inference?
06:20 Alex: no known gaps; SOC2 covers our control environment for the platform. we'll share the SOC2 Type II report; ISO 27001 summary is included too.
06:27 Ravi: do you provide contractual language for data processing addendum and subprocessor lists?
06:30 Alex: yes — DPA, subprocessors list and standard contractual clauses on request. we'll send our DPA and current subprocessor list.
06:38 Maya: curious about false positives in PII detection — if we mask names but keep clinical context, does that affect output quality?
06:45 Sam: it's a tradeoff — aggressive masking can reduce context and hurt quality; we recommend a hybrid approach: pre-send deterministic redaction for sensitive fields and use model-level prompts to preserve non-PII context. we'll pair engineering with you to design the pipeline for PHI-safe prompts.
06:59 Jordan: for PHI workloads we will likely want Private or Dedicated. what's the contract cadence and SLAs?
07:06 Alex: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime targets, reserved capacity and monthly or annual commits. Private is licensed with enterprise support; we'll share the SLA matrix.
07:15 Jordan: ok, can you also call out who from your side will be the single point of contact for security escalations?
07:19 Alex: lena will be your security engagement lead for onboarding, sam will be technical lead. i'll be overall account AE. we'll add escalation contacts in the docs.
07:27 Nina: any noisy transcripts or redaction failures to watch for? we've seen other vendors leak user identifiers in logs.
07:33 Sam: we continuously test for leakage; our logging pipeline supports configurable redaction and string pattern masking; for Dedicated/Private we recommend turning off content logging completely or piping logs to your own secure storage.
07:46 Jordan: do you have a retention policy for audit logs that meets healthcare e-discovery requirements?
07:50 Sam: we can extend retention to 7 years with enterprise add-ons; default isn't that long but we support it.
07:57 Ravi: legal wants a clause: indemnity if there's a breach caused by Redwood's negligence affecting PHI. is that typical?
08:03 Alex: we work with enterprise legal on indemnity clauses; terms vary by contract and level of engagement. we'll introduce legal to legal once you indicate intent.
08:11 Maya: latency vs encryption overhead — any perf numbers when using CMK and dedicated infra?
08:16 Sam: negligible crypto overhead for KMS calls; end-to-end latency impact is typically small (<5-15ms per request for KMS unwrap) but depends on region and key config. we'll share benchmark notes.
08:28 Jordan: can you run a short benchmark with our sample request set?
08:30 Alex: yes — next step: sam will run a dedicated benchmark, ideally on dedicated or private nodes, we'll need your sample prompts and region.
08:40 Jordan: i'll share a sanitized sample set, and note which prompts may contain PHI.
08:44 Sam: great.
08:46 Alex: quick recaps: sam sends SOC2/ISO and KMS notes; alex sends pricing/contract; customer to confirm region and pilot PHI needs; schedule SE deep dive.
08:58 Jordan: thanks, that's helpful. couple of quick clarifications — is there any scenario where raw prompts are replicated outside region for failover?
09:05 Sam: we can replicate metadata for failover, but raw prompt replication outside the configured region does not happen unless you enable cross-region replication. Failover can be region-local; we'll include our replication behavior in the doc.
09:17 Nina: and finally, how are backups of model parameters handled? any customer-specific snapshots?
09:22 Sam: model weights are managed by Redwood centrally; we do not snapshot customer prompts into model weight snapshots. customer-specific runtime artifacts (like caches) can be backed up per your policy in Dedicated/Private.
09:36 Jordan: ok sounds good. we'll need everything in writing for our security board.
09:40 Alex: understood. we'll get the pack out by friday.
09:44 Jordan: thanks everyone.
09:46 End of recording.
